facts.statement: The only known specimen of Nodocephalosaurus is a partial skull.
facts.quote: The type and only species, Nodocephalosaurus kirtlandensis, is known only from a partial skull.

facts.statement: Robert M. Sullivan named Nodocephalosaurus in 1999.
facts.quote: It was named in 1999 by Robert M. Sullivan.

facts.statement: Nodocephalosaurus was estimated to be 4.5 meters long and weigh 1.5 tonnes.
facts.quote: Nodocephalosaurus has an estimated length of 4.5 metres (15 feet) and weight of 1.5 tonnes (3,306 lbs).

facts.statement: The name Nodocephalosaurus means "knob-headed lizard" because of the bulbous osteoderms fused to the top of its skull.
facts.quote: The generic name, Nodocepahlosaurus, is derived from the Latin word "nodus" (knob or swelling ) and the Greek words "kephale" (head) and "sauros" (lizard), in reference to the many bulbous osteoderms fused to the top of the skull.

facts.statement: A partial skull of Nodocephalosaurus was discovered in 1995 in the De-na-zin member of the Kirtland Formation in New Mexico.
facts.quote: In 1995, a partial skull of an ankylosaur was discovered weathering out of a grey mudstone a few hundred metres west of a new Parasaurolophus site in the De-na-zin member of the Kirtland Formation, New Mexico.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Nodocephalosaurus is housed at the State Museum of Pennsylvania in Harrisburg.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen is currently housed at the State Museum of Pennsylvania, Harrisburg.

facts.statement: In 2000, Tracy Ford assigned a single pup-tent scute (NMMNH P-20880) to Nodocephalosaurus.
facts.quote: In 2000, Tracy Ford assigned NMMNH P-20880, a single pup-tent scute with a hollowed-out base, as a potential specimen of Nodocephalosaurus.

facts.statement: Arbour and Currie (2015) assigned most referred Nodocephalosaurus specimens to Ankylosauridae indet. after discovering other ankylosaurids in the same formation.
facts.quote: However, Arbour & Currie (2015) assigned all referred specimens, with the exception of SMPVP-1957, to Ankylosauridae indet. due to the discovery of Ahshislepelta in the Hunter Wash Member, and Ziapelta from the De-na-zin Member.

facts.statement: Sullivan originally diagnosed Nodocephalosaurus by bulbous osteoderms on the skull, a prominent quadratojugal horn, and a prominent post-maxillary/lacrimal osteoderm.
facts.quote: Sullivan (1999) originally diagnosed Nodocephalosaurus based on the presence of semi-inflated to bulbous polygonal osteoderms fused to the nasal, frontal and supraorbital regions of the skull, a prominent quadratojugal horn that is directed anteroventrally, and a prominent post-maxillary/lacrimal osteoderm.

facts.statement: The squamosal horns arch towards the back and terminate in a rounded point.
facts.quote: The squamosal horns arches towards the back, terminating in a rounded point.

facts.statement: Vickaryous et al. (2004) interpreted Nodocephalosaurus as Ankylosauridae incertae sedis.
facts.quote: Vickaryous et al. (2004) interpreted it as Ankylosauridae incertae sedis.

facts.statement: Nodocephalosaurus fossils come from the De-na-zin member of the Kirtland Formation.
facts.quote: Nodocephalosaurus is known from the De-na-zin member of the Kirtland Formation

facts.statement: The animal lived between 73.49 and 73.04 million years ago during the late Campanian to early Maastrichtian stages.
facts.quote: which has been dated to the upper-most Campanian to lower-most Maastrichtian stage, 73.49 ± 0.25 to 73.04 ± 0.25 Ma

facts.statement: It inhabited a floodplain on the western edge of the Western Interior Seaway rich in ferns, conifers, and flowering plants.
facts.quote: The Kirtland Formation lies on the western margin of the Western Interior Seaway and represents a floodplain that was abundant with ferns, conifers and flowering plants

facts.statement: Evidence suggests the environment had a warm temperate to subtropical climate.
facts.quote: Based on the abundance of angiosperms with leaves that have entire or nearly entire margins and drip points, the Kirtland Formation may have had a warm temperate to subtropical climate

facts.statement: Its presence indicates that ankylosaurids were more diverse than nodosaurids in the San Juan Basin.
facts.quote: The presence of Nodocephalosaurus and other ankylosaurids suggests that there was a higher diversity of ankylosaurids in the San Juan Basin than that of nodosaurids

facts.statement: Contemporary non-dinosaur species included a choristodere, crocodylomorphs like Denazinosuchus, several turtles, and fish such as Melvius and Myledaphus.
facts.quote: Non-dinosaur taxa contemporaneous with Nodocephalosaurus include an indeterminate choristodere, the crocodylomorphs Denazinosuchus, Brachychampsa and Leidyosuchus, the turtles Basilemys, Denazinemys, Neurankylus, Plastomenus and Thescelus, and the fishes Melvius and Myledaphus

facts.statement: It belongs to the subfamily Ankylosaurinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Ankylosaurinae

facts.statement: The animal is classified within the family Ankylosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Ankylosauridae

facts.statement: It is a member of the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: The genus was named by Sullivan in 1999.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Nodocephalosaurus (genus), Sullivan 1999

facts.statement: The genus existed from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago during the Campanian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Six fossil occurrences of this genus have been recorded.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 6
